notes:
Account snapshot: Scallop Harborware — mid-market productivity SaaS (workflow automation, integrated docs/chat). Mature product team: 350 employees, US HQ with EU customers. Currently on another LLM API provider (vendor: OpenAI) and exploring move to Redwood Hosted initially, then Dedicated reserved capacity in 2-4 quarters.

Recent activity / timeline:
- 2024-11-12: Intro demo with Daniel (AE) + Maya (SE). Showed Hosted API parity shim and streaming example. Fireflies ff_2024-11-12_3892.
- 2024-12-02: Security sync; sent SOC2 + KMS diagram; customer requested EU residency option for EU tenant data. Drive: security FAQ link shared.
- 2024-12-18: POC kickoff — 2-week compatibility layer test (OpenAI→Redwood Hosted). Objective: zero-touch prompt parity for chat and summarization flows; maintain streaming hooks; measure latency/cost.
- 2025-01-09: Mid-POC checkpoint — ran 1k summarization prompts (internal benchmark set). Noted 6% drop in abstractive-summary ROUGE-L vs baseline and slight change in tokenization behavior. Jira INF-2347 logged for regressions. Fireflies ff_2025-01-10_4421.
- 2025-01-15: Cost estimate review: Redwood Hosted lower per-token cost given batching + KV caching suggestions; potential 18-25% cost saving at current traffic if caching enabled.

Technical & requirements summary:
- Workloads: primarily chat-based product assistant, doc search embeddings for retrieval, and summarization for user-generated notes. Peak throughput ~25 req/s, typical p50 latency goal <= 250ms for short-chat completions.
- Model preference: open-model compatibility (gpt-like) but customer expects parity to their tuned OpenAI prompts. Must preserve streaming and function-calling semantics.
- Regression tolerance: product team requires <3% quality delta on key eval prompts for go/no-go. Current POC showing ~6% regression for summarization — need tuning or model variant adjustments.
- Routing/fallback: want Hosted→Dedicated migration path; also require automatic fallback to smaller model variant on Dedicated if capacity saturated.
- Security: SSO/SAML in place; strict audit logging and 1-year retention for user transcripts; EU data residency required for EU customer subset. KMS integration must be available for Dedicated.

POC results & technical notes:
- Compatibility shim: quick to map OpenAI request fields to Redwood Hosted endpoints; streaming hooks preserved with small change in chunk framing.
- Prompt parity tests: found tokenizer differences causing truncation on ~2% of prompts; created normalization layer in shim to pre-tokenize and pad prompts — mitigates many cases.
- Quality regressions: summarization variant on Redwood default model scored down; SE suggested trying alternate model family and applying small prompt engineering changes (system message tweaks).
- Latency: p50 under 220ms on Hosted in US region; p95 spikes when batch windows expand — Redwood Optimize recommendations suggest reducing batching window and enabling prefix caching for frequent docs.

Commercial & procurement notes:
- Current vendor commit runs through 2025-06 but customer open to staged migration (Hosted now, Dedicated contract for H2 2025). Estimated ARR if Dedicated wins = $75k-$225k depending on dedicated pool size and SLA tier. Finance requested full pricing scenario by 2025-01-27.

Next steps (short):
- SE (Maya) to run targeted A/B with alternate Redwood model families on summarization set by 2025-01-24.
- AE (Daniel) to provide detailed Dedicated pricing cadence and draft SOW for reserved capacity.
- Product/security: complete DPA/legal review and confirm EU residency approach for tenant partitioning.

Quotes / call snippets:
- "We need near-zero prompt regressions — users will notice summary drift." — PM lead (call 2025-01-09).
- "Cost saves look real if caching is seamless; we need harder numbers for committed spend." — Head of Ops.

Open questions / risks:
- How quickly can Redwood match their exact function-calling semantics used in prod?
- Legal: acceptable DPA language for EU customers; encryption-at-rest proof for Dedicated.
